Since `h` comes from the `site_settings` value `embeddable_hosts`, any host containing a single quote (or other SQL-significant characters) can break the migration or allow SQL injection during migratio

In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the code fetches `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy`. If the id is missing/invalid, `host` will be `nil`, leading to a `NoMethodError` when `save_host` does `host.host = ...` or when `destroy` calls `host.destroy`, causing a 500 instead of a controlled 404

In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the record is fetched via `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and may be `nil`. `save_host(host)` then immediately dereferences it (`host.host = ...`, `host.category_id = ...` at/around line 24), which will raise a `NoMethodError` for invalid/nonexistent IDs instead of returning a 404 or handled error.

In `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, the lookup is `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`. The DB side is lowercased but the bound parameter is not, so a referer like `http://Example.com` will produce `host = "Example.com"` and fail to match a stored `"example.com"` record. This makes allowed-host checks incorrectly case-sensitive.
